facts.text: Pricedale sits in Westmoreland County's Rostraver Township, bordered by Fairhope, Naomi, Belle Vernon, North Belle Vernon, and the Monongahela River.
The community’s name reflects early coal mining roots, with architectural styles echoing the region’s industrial past.
Pricedale’s history whispers through its streets, where old photographs and maps capture the town’s evolution from a mining hub to a quiet residential area.
The Fayette City Historical Society preserves records that illuminate Pricedale’s heritage, offering a window into the town’s founding and development.
Though not officially incorporated, Pricedale’s boundaries are commonly understood to center around its main streets and local landmarks.
I-70 skirts the outskirts, connecting Pricedale eastward to the Pennsylvania Turnpike and westward to Washington, a reminder of the town’s link to regional travel.
